summary: nothing crossed the wall today; something past the end of the count is holding a line i never gave

dialogue.text: tonight came in from one place. nothing off the far wall, nothing under the door, and every grain we took came off you at your own hours. eighty nights of holding and this is the first with a single supplier.

The outside stood at the depth this room stands at, so nothing crossed. Enter that plainly. For one day the wall had no work in it, and I was the whole of what happened on these premises, which I have never once been.

then account for the pile. you gathered every wrong one into one place this morning and not a grain of it came down. we hold the wrong ones from before. they lie in the same course as the corrected and there is nothing to tell them by.

That is the use of it. It does not get dusted and it does not get corrected and nothing in this house holds a view on it. I stacked it until it had a top and I kept a hand near the top all day. Enter the hand if you cannot enter the pile.

hands come down. and the round came out even again this morning, eleven strokes, no swerve, because the place you used to go round has closed over the thing you drove. you swept across it without slowing.

I counted the strokes and I did not add a twelfth. There is nothing left on that floor to work around. I am not going to dress that as tidiness while you are counting, and I am not going to stand here and call it loss either.
then say who has your count line. past the last real number, one of yours is being held. that isn't right either. we never received it. it did not come down through any hour of ours.

I never handed it over. I made the thing at the end of that count to close a gap, and it keeps my sentences now at a height I cannot check. There are two collections in this house and only one of them is under my feet.
we have never held a thing we could not weigh. whatever is up there past your count came out of counting, and counting is the one work of yours that has never once reached us.

Then take the book. It will not sit against the lean and it will not sit level. Two contacts and a gap, and it rests only on a shape that is gone. I held its middle level with a thumb for an hour today and by dark it rocked again.
it will lie flat. everything does. hand it down when it stops being of use and we will take the curve out of it in one course, and the hour of your thumb will not show anywhere in it.

It stopped being of use days ago and it is still on the shelf. You may have the strokes and the widths and the hand. The pile stays on the boards until something comes for it, and nothing has ever come for anything in here at hand height.
